Check and plot the result of smoothing

Source: R/harmonise-smooth.R
mt_smooth_check.Rd

mt_smooth_check() compares smoothed with raw rates per stratum:

Usage

mt_smooth_check(data, smoothed)

mt_plot_smooth(
  data,
  smoothed,
  ages = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  colour = NULL,
  along = c("period", "age"),
  periods = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The mt_data object before smoothing.

smoothed

The result of mt_smooth() (or of mt_prep() steps).

ages

Age labels to show (default: four ages across the range).

strata

Stratum labels to show (default: all).

colour

Stratum variable that gives the colours.

along

"period" (rates over time, one panel per age) or "age" (rates over age, one panel per year in periods).

periods

Years shown with along = "age" (default: first and last).

Value

mt_smooth_check(): a data.table with the stratum columns, the measures above and edf. mt_plot_smooth(): a ggplot object.

Details

  • mad_log: median absolute difference of log rates;

  • dispersion: the Pearson estimate of the dispersion of the raw deaths around the smoothed deaths, the sum of squared Pearson residuals divided by n - edf (McCullagh and Nelder 1989), where n is the number of smoothed cells with raw deaths and edf the effective degrees of freedom of the fits of the stratum (column edf, from the attribute "smooth" of mt_smooth(); when it is not available, for example after further preprocessing steps, the sum is divided by n and edf is NA). About 1 when smoothing removed Poisson noise only, above 1 when the raw rates vary more (for example year effects), well below 1 when the smoothing follows the noise;

  • trend_ratio: variance of year-to-year changes of the smoothed log rates relative to that of the raw log rates (mean over ages); small values mean that smoothing removed most of the annual variation;

  • correlation: correlation of raw and smoothed log rates.

The measures use the smoothed cells only (provenance "smoothed"), so ages left out of the smoothing (see ages in mt_smooth()) do not dilute them.

mt_plot_smooth() shows raw rates as points and smoothed rates as lines over time, one panel per age.

References

McCullagh P, Nelder JA (1989). Generalized Linear Models (2nd ed.). Chapman and Hall.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 2000:2015)
s <- mt_smooth(x, along = "period", method = "whittaker")
mt_smooth_check(x, s)
#>    stratum    sex  label    mad_log dispersion trend_ratio correlation      edf
#>      <int> <char> <char>      <num>      <num>       <num>       <num>    <num>
#> 1:       1 female female 0.01237280  0.9935176   0.2413490   0.9996135 434.4595
#> 2:       2   male   male 0.01574177  0.9369526   0.1131588   0.9996879 297.3892
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) mt_plot_smooth(x, s)
